paper-2610.22744.title: OmniXRef: A Unified Framework for Multimodal Multi-Reference Video Editing
paper-2610.22744.summary: Creative intent in video editing can be expressed through text instructions (e.g., "remove the people"), image references (e.g., subject appearance), video references (e.g., camera movement), or a combination of the above.

paper-2610.22791.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
paper-2610.22791.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown promising potential in coding tasks, and their performance is jointly determined by the policy model and the harness that mediates their interaction with the environment.

paper-2610.22894.title: Competence-Based Evaluation of Logical Reasoning in Large Language Models
paper-2610.22894.summary: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have brought impressive performance across diverse tasks; however, shortcomings remain in logical reasoning, including inconsistencies under linguistic variation.

paper-2610.23010.title: What Makes a Good Symbol for Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Planning?
paper-2610.23010.summary: The physical world has continuous state and action spaces, yet robot planning often benefits from hybrid discrete-continuous formulations that explicitly expose combinatorial structure, such as contact modes or discrete primitive actions.

paper-2610.23036.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent-State Design
paper-2610.23036.summary: Looped language models reuse physical Transformer blocks across logical depth, but established architectures entangle recurrence placement, input injection, and recurrent state organization.

paper-2610.23121.title: Scene-Designer: Learning Design Intelligence for Agentic 3D Scene Generation
paper-2610.23121.summary: Generating complete, coherent, and usable 3D indoor scenes from natural language requires strong design intelligence: the ability to design high-quality scenes and critique their quality.

paper-2610.23181.title: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper-2610.23181.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has become a scalable post-training paradigm for large language models.

paper-2610.23194.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence
paper-2610.23194.summary: AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments.

paper-2610.23230.title: RAP: A Dataset for Paper-to-Poster Generation via Declarative Markup from Human-Crafted Exemplars
paper-2610.23230.summary: Making a conference poster is visual coding in miniature: an entire paper must be compressed onto a single page, which exercises summarization, visual design, and code implementation at once, using nothing beyond the paper itself.

paper-2610.23279.title: Xiaomi-Lens-0 Technical Report
paper-2610.23279.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) answer questions about whole images well, yet they still struggle with fine-grained region understanding. A key reason is that text-only supervision never specifies which regions support an answer.

paper-2610.23344.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
paper-2610.23344.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language-model (LM) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self-improvement.

paper-2610.23374.title: MOSS-Image Technical Report
paper-2610.23374.summary: Recent closed-source image generation systems can produce diverse visual content from simple compositions to information-dense graphics, yet open-weight text-to-image models still struggle with dense text and intricate layouts.

paper-2610.23400.title: On the Tip of the Tongue: First-Token Cueing as a Behavioral Probe of Recall Failures in LLMs
paper-2610.23400.summary: Large language models often answer factual questions incorrectly in closed-book settings, and such errors are usually attributed to missing knowledge. Yet models often encode answers they fail to produce.

paper-2610.23470.title: QD-Rec: Open-Ended Evolution of Recommendations via Quality-Diversity
paper-2610.23470.summary: Open-ended search combined with foundation models has produced advances such as faster algorithms, new results on open mathematical problems, and self-improving agents.

paper-2610.23479.title: HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents
paper-2610.23479.summary: Agents built on vision language models (VLMs) now compete with learned policies on robot manipulation leaderboards. We ask how far a coding agent can go when it controls a robot instead of a computer, and where it stops.

paper-2610.23542.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models
paper-2610.23542.summary: A memory test for a video world model should say whether the scene was set, whether the asked change was carried out, and whether the last frame shows the result. Current tests fold these into one number, so a low score is easy to read as forgetting.

paper-2610.23600.title: Learning to Discriminate Scene Structures Makes Self-Supervised Depth Learning Scalable
paper-2610.23600.summary: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation is appealing for its potential to scale with unlabeled data, yet existing methods often degrade when trained on diverse scenes.

paper-2610.23653.title: A Language-Informed Loss for Visual Generation
paper-2610.23653.summary: End-to-end visual generation with pixel-space loss has recently achieved competitive performance without the need for learned image tokenizers.

paper-2610.23751.title: MTEdit: Packed Trajectories Beat Rollouts for Multi-Turn Image Editing
paper-2610.23751.summary: Multi-turn image editing aims to modify an image according to a sequence of instructions, making it better aligned with human-AI collaborative creation than single-turn editing.

paper-2610.23787.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
paper-2610.23787.summary: Speculative decoding has become a mainstream technique for accelerating large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight draft model to generate candidate tokens that are subsequently verified by the target model.

paper-2610.23795.title: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
paper-2610.23795.summary: Video world models that generate and explore environments at scale need a persistent 3D memory of what they have produced.

paper-2610.23839.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
paper-2610.23839.summary: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging.

paper-2610.23841.title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
paper-2610.23841.summary: Pretrained VLMs bring rich world knowledge and semantic priors to object-goal navigation, and fine-tuning a VLM into a navigation policy has become a common recipe.

paper-2610.23935.title: Factorization-Guided Training and Inference for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding
paper-2610.23935.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference through parallel verification of tokens proposed by a drafter.

paper-2610.23986.title: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
paper-2610.23986.summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled them to act as autonomous agents, creating and editing 3D models via code or direct software manipulation.

paper-2610.24087.title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
paper-2610.24087.summary: Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation?

paper-2610.24133.title: A Conditional No-Hair Theorem for Transformers: How Language Models Forget Their Prompt
paper-2610.24133.summary: We ask how much an autoregressive transformer retains of its prompt after generating t tokens.

paper-2610.24452.title: HumanSkill-4D: Training-Free Language Querying of Animatable Gaussian Avatars in Space and Time
paper-2610.24452.summary: We introduce avatar referring segmentation, which selects regions of animatable Gaussian avatars from language queries. A query can also specify a pose or motion to select matching intervals.

paper-2610.24519.title: Axiomatic World Modeling for Physics Reasoning
paper-2610.24519.summary: Recent research-level physics-reasoning benchmarks for LLMs reveal a failure mode that lies not in knowledge or execution, but in modeling the world being reasoned about.

paper-2610.24611.title: HSPR: Recovering Software-Agent Benchmark Scores via Hierarchical Posterior Inference
paper-2610.24611.summary: Evaluating software agents on a full benchmark is expensive. A small task subset can preserve agent rankings while yielding inaccurate scores.

paper-2610.24628.title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model
paper-2610.24628.summary: We introduce Muse Glimmer, an open-source 30B parameter causal language model with perception encoder, purpose-built for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware.

paper-2610.24648.title: EdgeKernelBench: Unified LLM-Driven Kernel Generation for Edge Backends
paper-2610.24648.summary: Recent works show that LLMs can generate kernels with strong performance on server GPUs. Edge deployment presents distinct challenges because the hardware is heterogeneous, the software stacks are fragmented, and the resource budgets are tight.

paper-2610.24649.title: Good Judgment, Bad Advice: Decision-Model Controllers Raise Agent Cost Without Improving Success
paper-2610.24649.summary: Agent scaffolds increasingly delegate small decisions (whether to stop, verify, or change approach) to cheaper models.

paper-2610.24766.title: ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion Beyond Auxiliary Multi-Token Prediction
paper-2610.24766.summary: Existing Multi-token prediction (MTP) methods are auxiliary by design: the multi-horizon loss mostly trains modules attached to the backbone, and each added horizon costs another module and another pass.

paper-2610.24771.title: Design Anything, Design at Scale
paper-2610.24771.summary: As multimodal resources are transformed into media outputs, agentic AI is expected to stay aligned with design intent over long horizons. Designers follow briefs specifying goals, constraints, and deliverables, with later work building on earlier decisions.

paper-2610.24791.title: UniAVC: Unified Audio-Video Creation via Progressive Training and Asymmetric Scheduling
paper-2610.24791.summary: Unified audio-video creation requires a single model capable of text-conditioned joint synthesis, bidirectional cross-modal generation, and instruction-guided editing across both modalities.

paper-2610.24899.title: HybridResearcher: Bridging the Structured-Unstructured Boundary for Deep Research Agents
paper-2610.24899.summary: While LLM agents are increasingly capable of gathering and synthesizing evidence from a single homogeneous source, such as structured tables or unstructured data, real-world analytical questions frequently span heterogeneous sources.

paper-2610.24944.title: Epi: Towards a Persistent, Self-Improving Agent for Autonomous Research
paper-2610.24944.summary: We present Épi, an autonomous research agent that sustains investigations across model sessions and evolves its methods through accumulated experience.

paper-2610.24960.title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents
paper-2610.24960.summary: AI coworkers must coordinate tools, communicate across turns, and act on changing workspace state while respecting workflow constraints.

paper-2610.25011.title: FineSplat: Fine Patches, Local Groups, Detailed Splats
paper-2610.25011.summary: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) promises instant scene reconstruction with high-quality novel-view synthesis.

paper-2610.25043.title: VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse
paper-2610.25043.summary: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models generate an action chunk by iteratively denoising Gaussian noise, but typically execute only a short prefix before replanning with updated observations.

paper-2610.25060.title: Policy Is Not Capability: Some Safety Benchmarks Measure Which Definition of "Unsafe" You Trained On
paper-2610.25060.summary: A guardrail classifier is reported as if unsafe were a property of text. It is not: it is a property of a policy, and the policy enters the model through its labels.

paper-2610.25078.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
paper-2610.25078.summary: Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities.

paper-2610.25090.title: Think Visually Across Space and Time: Grounded Reasoning for Video Segmentation
paper-2610.25090.summary: Video Reasoning Segmentation (VRS) requires a model to identify an implicitly described target and predict its pixel-level mask trajectory, while resolving the spatial relations and temporal events that determine the answer.

paper-2610.25159.title: Legal Guidance in the Wild: How Users Seek Legal Help in Real-World LLM Conversations
paper-2610.25159.summary: People ask conversational AI models about their legal rights, obligations, procedures, and personal situations that may have legal consequences.

paper-2610.25265.title: SPARC: Spoken Profile Authorship Recognition Corpus
paper-2610.25265.summary: Speech anonymization has focused on the acoustic signal, leaving open how much speaker information the transcribed words themselves retain. In this work, we study pairwise speaker and demographic-attribute verification from transcribed speech.

paper-2610.25288.title: Vision as Proprioception: Estimating Humanoid Robot Pose from Video
paper-2610.25288.summary: Estimating a humanoid robot's internal state from video has a wide range of real-world applications but remains unexplored.

paper-2610.25296.title: World Model Interpretability: From Decoding Representations to Understanding Latent Worlds
paper-2610.25296.summary: Emerging Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) are moving beyond representation learning towards latent world models that support prediction, planning, and control. Yet their latent worlds naturally lack a human-interpretable interface.

paper-2610.25369.title: Painting Change Map as guidance for generating painting processes
paper-2610.25369.summary: Digital art generation has undergone a massive paradigm shift, moving from static image synthesis to dynamic video generation that can mimic the human painting process.

paper-2610.25404.title: MT Forcing: Towards Stable and Consistent Multi-Turn Image Editing with Autoregressive Diffusion
paper-2610.25404.summary: Multi-turn image editing aims to modify an image according to a sequence of instructions, enabling more effective interactive visual content creation for users.

paper-2610.25459.title: BiDex-100: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Across 100+ Simulation Tasks
paper-2610.25459.summary: Bimanual manipulation with dexterous hands has attracted growing attention in research on robotic action models.

paper-2610.25519.title: ATEST: Adaptive Resource-Aware Test-Time Scaling for LLM Inference
paper-2610.25519.summary: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves large language model (LLM) reasoning by sampling multiple answers, but fixed sampling budgets ignore both query difficulty and the changing energy cost of inference under GPU contention.

paper-2610.25525.title: StopLoss: Teaching Agents to Predict Failure and Stop Early
paper-2610.25525.summary: Coding agents keep working on runs that will fail verification, and asking a frontier model to watch for this is expensive in its own right.

paper-2610.25666.title: Frechet Forcing: Training Long-Horizon Streaming World Models from Short Clips
paper-2610.25666.summary: Streaming video world models generate the future chunk by chunk, conditioned on their own past and a stream of actions. Trained on short clips, they drift once a rollout exceeds the training horizon, as prediction errors re-enter the context and compound.

paper-2610.25690.title: ScaleNav: Scalable Internet Video Pretraining for Language-Conditioned Local Navigation
paper-2610.25690.summary: We study language-conditioned local navigation, where a robot must navigate to a text-specified target visible in its initial observation and stop at the described location.

paper-2610.25736.title: Learning from Fleet Experience: A Collective Learning Paradigm for Robots
paper-2610.25736.summary: Experience generated during deployment offers an opportunity for robots to improve policy reliability through learning from their own executions.

paper-2610.25765.title: TRACE: Tracking Multimodal Clinical Trajectories for Inpatient Risk Prediction
paper-2610.25765.summary: Accurate inpatient risk prediction requires modeling heterogeneous clinical evidence that accumulates irregularly over time. This challenge spans in-hospital mortality, prolonged length of stay, and readmission, each with task-specific observation windows.

paper-2610.25844.title: SWIFT: Self-guided Weak-to-strong dIFfusion models via Target extrapolation
paper-2610.25844.summary: Training high-quality diffusion models is computationally expensive, and inference-time guidance often adds further sampling cost.

paper-2610.25861.title: ActionRoPE: action as coordinates for spatially consistent control in planar-camera game world models
paper-2610.25861.summary: Game world models have made rapid progress toward real-time interactive generation. Yet action control is still predominantly implemented as feature conditioning, leaving the model to learn from training data how each action should move the visual world.

paper-2610.25874.title: Vision-Language-Delta-Action: Learning Compact Deltas as Actionable Transition Interfaces for Robotic Manipulation
paper-2610.25874.summary: Robotic manipulation is not merely observation-to-action generation, but the realization of task-specified state changes in the physical world.

paper-2610.25950.title: AdaExploreBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Proactive Exploration and Test-time Adaptation in Evolving Environments
paper-2610.25950.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in unfamiliar and evolving environments, requiring them to proactively explore, understand, and adapt to environmental dynamics.

paper-2610.25964.title: Token-Set Choice Confounds POPE: A Systematic Audit of Yes/No Extraction in VLM Hallucination Evaluation
paper-2610.25964.summary: We set out to reproduce a recent hallucination-mitigation result on the POPE benchmark.

paper-2610.26067.title: PhysSkin++: Real-Time and Generalizable Physics-Based Animation via Self-Supervised Neural Skinning
paper-2610.26067.summary: Generalizing real-time physics-based animation across diverse 3D shapes and spatial discretizations remains challenging.

paper-2610.26081.title: DeOverlay: A Benchmark and Source-Anchored Flow for Video Overlay Removal
paper-2610.26081.summary: Video overlay removal aims to recover scenes obscured by subtitles, titles, and logos while preserving surrounding content.

paper-2610.26203.title: Focused Omni-Modal GUI Agents
paper-2610.26203.summary: Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents increasingly act over streaming omni-modal observations spanning screenshots, audio, video, interaction history, and device states.

paper-2610.26216.title: RoAR-VAE: Improving Latent Diffusability through Robust Prediction
paper-2610.26216.summary: An effective visual tokenizer must preserve image fidelity while producing latents that downstream diffusion models can learn efficiently. Prior work improves latent diffusability through semantic alignment or joint tokenizer--diffusion training.

paper-2610.26397.title: Bridged Self-Distillation for On-Policy Learning
paper-2610.26397.summary: On-policy distillation can transfer the reasoning capabilities of a strong teacher to a smaller student.

paper-2610.26426.title: HarnessRL: Co-Evolving Policies with a Just-in-Time Training Harness for Open-Ended RL
paper-2610.26426.summary: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) trains policies for open-ended generation with natural-language criteria as rewards, but these rewards can become ineffective as training progresses. We identify two failure modes.

paper-2610.26453.title: Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints
paper-2610.26453.summary: Lifelong agents continually accumulate and reuse experience to improve after deployment, yet in practice they often operate under tight generation, interaction, and memory budgets.

paper-2610.26542.title: Breaking Diffusion: Parallel Reasoning with Draft Refinement
paper-2610.26542.summary: Drafting an answer allows a reasoning model to reconsider each decision in the context of the others. Yet repeated diffusion denoising does not ensure that individually plausible token updates form a better answer together.

paper-2610.26549.title: Holi-World: Building Holistic World Intelligence from Human-Ego Experience
paper-2610.26549.summary: Human egocentric experience offers a rich foundation for learning how the world is organized and how it changes through interaction.

paper-2610.26625.title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience
paper-2610.26625.summary: Reconstructing human activity from egocentric video requires more than recovering individual 3D components: the observer's motion, surrounding geometry, and hand-object interactions must fit together in a consistent world.

paper-2610.26659.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
paper-2610.26659.summary: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world.

paper-2610.26663.title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models
paper-2610.26663.summary: Robotic value models assess task execution from visual observations and instructions, providing feedback for policy learning and execution monitoring.

paper-2610.26681.title: From Short Clips to Real-Time Streams: Identity-Aware Supervision and Context-Efficient Generation for Video Face Swapping
paper-2610.26681.summary: Video face swapping transfers the reference identity to a target video while preserving its other attributes and motion.

paper-2610.26711.title: PVBench: Quantifying Physical Plausibility in Video Generation with Object-Level Physical Measurements
paper-2610.26711.summary: Recent video generation models produce visually compelling outputs, yet their physical plausibility remains poorly measured. Physical plausibility asks whether generated objects obey geometry, kinematics, dynamics, and conservation laws.

paper-2610.26754.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
paper-2610.26754.summary: Expert human readers process large inputs (e.g., code repositories and long documents) by skimming to closely read only what matters.

paper-2610.26765.title: HandsOn: A Large-Scale Simulation Benchmark for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation
paper-2610.26765.summary: General-purpose manipulation requires reliable behavior across embodiments, objects, and task demands. We introduce HandsOn, a composable simulation platform and benchmark for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation.

paper-2610.26770.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
paper-2610.26770.summary: Harness development plays a crucial role in building capable AI agents. Recent approaches improve harnesses through recursive self-improvement (RSI), but their performance gains often come with higher execution costs.

paper-2610.26802.title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding
paper-2610.26802.summary: Brain encoding models aim to predict neural responses to stimuli. The most widely used approach fits readouts from frozen pretrained backbones.

paper-2610.26811.title: State World Models: Execute the Rules, Generate the Pixels
paper-2610.26811.summary: Existing world models can generate action-conditioned video from a single image. Many focus on camera movement, allowing users to explore the generated scene.

paper-2610.26824.title: SpecMRL: Redesign Matryoshka Representation Learning within Parametric Spectrum
paper-2610.26824.summary: Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) is designed to support flexible representation sizes by jointly optimizing nested prefixes.

paper-2610.26825.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
paper-2610.26825.summary: Memory-native evolution requires making memory an intrinsic capability of foundation models, enabling them to continuously accumulate and utilize information.

paper-2610.26828.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
paper-2610.26828.summary: Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks.

paper-2610.26830.title: Competing Learning in Hybrid Architectures
paper-2610.26830.summary: Many modern language models have adopted hybrid architectures that incorporate both linear-time recurrence and softmax attention.

paper-2610.26834.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention
paper-2610.26834.summary: We propose KronLSTM, a linear attention architecture based on the Kronecker Delta Rule, a novel update rule for associative matrix memories.

paper-2610.26837.title: SpecKCast: Spectral Kalman Forecasting for Diffusion Acceleration
paper-2610.26837.summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve high-fidelity image and video generation, but they suffer from substantial inference costs due to repeated transformer evaluations across many denoising steps.

paper-2610.26844.title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts
paper-2610.26844.summary: The goal of a world model is to capture the dynamics of an environment. This has the great appeal that it allows agents to plan and simulate a course of actions with the help of a world model.

paper-2610.26848.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
paper-2610.26848.summary: In this paper, we systematically investigate the mechanisms, scaling behavior, and generalization of physical Recursive self-improvement.

paper-2610.26851.title: Manga2Animate: An Agentic Framework for Faithful Manga Animation with Script and Storyboard Planning
paper-2610.26851.summary: Adapting existing manga into coherent animation that stays faithful to the source is a valuable yet challenging task.

paper-2610.26853.title: InfiniDream: Open-Ended Photorealistic 3D Worlds Through Procedural Generation
paper-2610.26853.summary: Procedural generation plays a key role in synthetic data creation and game development, offering greater controllability, editability, and diversity than static mesh representations.

paper-2610.26855.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
paper-2610.26855.summary: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision.

paper-2610.26857.title: VideoMaMa++: Temporally Consistent Video Matting via Preserve-and-Refine Token
paper-2610.26857.summary: Diffusion-based video matting has recently emerged as a leading approach, leveraging video diffusion priors from internet-scale pretraining to achieve strong zero-shot generalization from limited synthetic data.

paper-2610.26860.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
paper-2610.26860.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress on visual reasoning, yet many tasks require evidence that is difficult to obtain through internal reasoning alone: our controlled study on 22 benchmarks shows that simply increasing the inferen…

paper-2610.26863.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
paper-2610.26863.summary: Modern text-to-image (T2I) systems use internet-scale language pretraining for text-conditioned image generation. We ask whether language pretraining is necessary for strong T2I generation.

paper-2610.27040.title: ACE-Brain-0.6: Scaling Spatial Grounding for Physical Foundation Models
paper-2610.27040.summary: General-purpose multimodal models, including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, demonstrate broad capabilities in embodied manipulation.

paper-2610.27190.title: On the Fragility of Tasks under Composition: Implicit Budgeting in Language Models
paper-2610.27190.summary: Modern language models are increasingly asked to handle several tasks within a single prompt. Doing so requires solving each task correctly while integrating the resulting answers into a coherent response.

paper-2610.27227.title: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams
paper-2610.27227.summary: Cooperative language-model agents can improve without weight updates by revising reusable skills, but only if a shared team reward is traced to the responsible agent and skill.

paper-2610.27327.title: Unsupervised Tool Evolution for Coding Agents in Data-Lake Analytics
paper-2610.27327.summary: Coding agents can answer analytical questions over a data lake by discovering, cleaning, and joining the relevant data. However, they discard this work after each question and redo it from scratch for the next one.

paper-2610.27334.title: EMBER: Predicting TCR--pMHC Binding Without a Docked Complex
paper-2610.27334.summary: We propose EMBER, a structure-based framework for TCR--pMHC binding prediction that eliminates the need for a predicted docked complex, and with it the placement error that dominates such predictions.

paper-2610.27360.title: On the Limits of Scale: Inverse Scaling in Vision-Language Models
paper-2610.27360.summary: Scaling laws suggest that increasing model size, training data, and compute generally yields monotonic performance improvements.

paper-2610.27406.title: More Memory, Worse Agents: Error Reproduction and Anti-Persistence in LLM Agents
paper-2610.27406.summary: LLM agents can improve across tasks without updating model parameters by storing experience from their own executions in external memory and reusing it to guide later decisions.

paper-2610.27435.title: Harness Self-Evolution for Long-Horizon Terminal Agents
paper-2610.27435.summary: Long-horizon terminal agents may solve a task in one run yet fail across repeated runs. Stochastic errors can propagate through actions and context, creating a gap between capability and reliable execution.

paper-2610.27450.title: Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation
paper-2610.27450.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) can succeed with surprisingly few training questions, motivating a view of questions as carriers of distributional knowledge transfer.

paper-2610.27592.title: Real In, Real Out: What If We Only Use Real Data for Scene Text Editing?
paper-2610.27592.summary: Aiming to modify textual content while preserving the original style, Scene Text Editing (STE) has significant practical value in many applications. STE typically requires paired images before and after editing for training.

paper-2610.27628.title: PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking
paper-2610.27628.summary: Looped language models can run more iterations at test time, but additional iterations need not help them solve longer problems.

paper-2610.27861.title: RoboCasa-Shift: Stage-Aware Robustness Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Policies in Long-Horizon Household Manipulation
paper-2610.27861.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) robustness is commonly summarized by aggregate task success, which obscures how individual executions change under distribution shifts and where failures emerge in long-horizon tasks.

paper-2610.27911.title: MMEnterprise-Bench: Evaluating Enterprise Agents over Evolving Multimodal Records
paper-2610.27911.summary: Enterprise agents answer questions over workplace records that evolve through team collaboration. As information is shared, corrected, and revised across documents, chats, and figures, multiple versions of the same information accumulate in the workspace.

paper-2610.27914.title: World Models with Configurable Perception
paper-2610.27914.summary: Real-world observations are noisy and often contain excessive task-irrelevant information. Effective world modeling and planning need to abstract observations into world state representations while filtering out irrelevant information.

paper-2610.27999.title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
paper-2610.27999.summary: Moving from controllable videos to genuinely playable worlds requires persistent world state, executable game rules, and low-latency interaction.

paper-2610.28027.title: From RL Papers to Framework Code: Inclusion and Review in Seven Open-Source Training Frameworks
paper-2610.28027.summary: Practitioners use reinforcement learning methods for language models through training frameworks, so a method that a framework includes is one configuration change away for its users. We measure how often this happens.

paper-2610.28069.title: Training the Whole Agent, Not Just the Model
paper-2610.28069.summary: Training coding agents typically updates the policy while keeping the harness fixed. During training, trajectories reveal flawed repair strategies and interaction problems that vary across tasks and change as the policy learns.

paper-2610.28074.title: Slot-JEPA: Object-Structured Prediction Interfaces for Latent World Models
paper-2610.28074.summary: As a prototypical latent world model, Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) provide strong semantic representations.

paper-2610.28284.title: HRoPE: Homography Relative Positional Encoding
paper-2610.28284.summary: Geometric Relative Positional Encoding has become the primary mechanism for injecting spatial inductive biases into multi-view transformers.

paper-2610.28354.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
paper-2610.28354.summary: Spatial reasoning asks a model to work out where objects are in 3D space, how they relate to one another, and how they move.

paper-2610.28388.title: Self-Credit: Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Agentic RL via Intra-group Rescaling
paper-2610.28388.summary: LLM agents are commonly trained with RLVR, but the sparse nature of typical RLVR rewards makes credit assignment challenging, especially for long-horizon tasks.

paper-2610.28402.title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
paper-2610.28402.summary: As streaming video generation advances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important.

paper-2610.28435.title: Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision
paper-2610.28435.summary: Multimodal rerankers are usually dedicated models: a vision-language model (VLM) is trained on retrieval data to score the candidates of a query. Scoring options is not specific to reranking.

paper-2610.28441.title: Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity
paper-2610.28441.summary: Large Language Model inference over long contexts is increasingly bottlenecked by the cost of attending to a growing Key-Value (KV) cache.

paper-2610.28444.title: EvaOmni: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Audio-Visual Reasoning
paper-2610.28444.summary: Omni LLMs can naturally locate key audio and visual evidence and integrate information across modalities for audiovisual reasoning.

paper-2610.28474.title: Answering in the User's Variety: Calibrated Accommodation Pairs for Post-Training
paper-2610.28474.summary: People adapt how they talk to the person in front of them. However, chat models tend to respond in Standard English regardless of the dialect used by the user.

paper-2610.28522.title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems
paper-2610.28522.summary: Decision models support routing, guardrails, and output verification in LLM systems. However, item accuracy alone cannot establish whether models make correct decisions across controlled variations or assign reliable confidence to their predictions.

paper-2610.28554.title: OverSeer: Multi-Agent World Models Beyond What Agents See
paper-2610.28554.summary: Despite the success of video world models, extending them to multiple agents is difficult because it requires generating several agent-specific video streams that are consistent in time and between agents.

paper-2610.28559.title: Large Flow Language Models
paper-2610.28559.summary: Continuous flow language models offer a path to parallel generation with tools for control and acceleration unavailable to discrete diffusion, yet effective techniques for building them at the billion-parameter scale remain less established.

paper-2610.28577.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
paper-2610.28577.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents can handle increasingly complex tasks, navigating long trajectories of observations and actions. As these trajectories grow, key-value (KV) cache I/O and storage become the dominant cost.

paper-2610.28578.title: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
paper-2610.28578.summary: In this report, we introduce Sage-A1.5, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model that builds on A1 to advance long-horizon problem solving through adaptive capability composition.

paper-2610.28589.title: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics
paper-2610.28589.summary: Agentic robotics systems combine planners with robot harnesses to perform complex manipulation tasks.

paper-2610.28594.title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
paper-2610.28594.summary: Reliable multi-view forecasting requires videos from different cameras to describe the same evolving 3D scene.

paper-2610.28601.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
paper-2610.28601.summary: Computer-use agents are limited by the interfaces humans give them. An agent may type a spreadsheet cell by cell when a single line of code would do, or print all two thousand lines of a file through a shell to find one function.

paper-2610.28630.title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
paper-2610.28630.summary: Game engines and coding agents can specify the layout, motion, and camera of a scene, yet turning such coarse structure into realistic video requires a renderer that follows the structure and completes the appearance it leaves open.

paper-2610.28632.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
paper-2610.28632.summary: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene.

paper-2610.28679.title: VerifierBench: Benchmarking the Generation of Executable Verifiers for LLM Agents
paper-2610.28679.summary: Agents need reliable ways to validate their outputs, both when completing tasks and when filtering synthetic training data.

paper-2610.28698.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
paper-2610.28698.summary: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws.

paper-2610.28711.title: Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR Technical Report
paper-2610.28711.summary: We present Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR, a family of audio-language models that builds upon its predecesor Qwen-Audio-3.0-ASR with improved speech recognition and expanded capabilities in speaker-diarized transcription and general audio understanding.

paper-2610.28763.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
paper-2610.28763.summary: Frontier coding agents are increasingly framed as end-to-end automated researchers, and ML for science offers a demanding test of that promise: improving a scientific model often requires domain insight beyond routine ML engineering.

paper-2610.28827.title: WorldStream: Streaming Interactive 3D Worlds with Hierarchical Planning and Persistent State
paper-2610.28827.summary: We present WorldStream, an open-ended 3D world model with three simultaneous capabilities: it extends playable terrain beyond any pre-specified map, acts on open-ended language in the running world, and restores visited places with their edits.

paper-2610.28887.title: Building AI Research Teams for Autonomous Discovery of Linear Attention Architectures
paper-2610.28887.summary: Autonomous agents can increasingly propose ideas, modify code, and run experiments, creating an opportunity to accelerate scientific discovery using teams of collaborative AI researchers.

paper-2610.28905.title: Hidden Messages Between Diffusion Language Model Agents: Causal Evidence for Latent Communication
paper-2610.28905.summary: Diffusion language models form answers through a sequence of revisable continuous states, but multi-agent systems usually discard those states and make agents communicate only after decoding text.

paper-2610.28909.title: DiffResearch: Accelerating Deep Research with Diffusion Language Models
paper-2610.28909.summary: Deep research systems iteratively plan, gather evidence, synthesize, and revise, making end-to-end latency a key bottleneck for interactive use.

paper-2610.28940.title: StyleStream 2.0: Fast and Controllable Streaming Voice Style Conversion
paper-2610.28940.summary: Voice style conversion (VSC) aims to transform a source utterance to match the timbre, accent, and emotion of a target voice while preserving linguistic content.

paper-2610.29317.title: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience
paper-2610.29317.summary: Spatial reasoning requires more than access to geometric tools: a reasoner must decide when direct observation is sufficient and when to reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames.

paper-2610.29357.title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
paper-2610.29357.summary: Autonomous agents powered by foundation models can reason, plan, and use tools, but their fixed weights and context limits hinder sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment.

paper-2610.29434.title: RubatoCodec: Budgeted Adaptive Speech Tokenization with Streaming Decoding
paper-2610.29434.summary: Neural speech codecs provide discrete tokens for speech generation. Lower frame rates shorten token sequences, but each token must then carry more linguistic and acoustic information.

paper-2610.29441.title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
paper-2610.29441.summary: Full 3D attention is costly in video Diffusion Transformers. Block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing only selected attention blocks.

paper-2610.29458.title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper-2610.29458.summary: Agent harnesses have become a central component of modern agentic systems, shaping how models use tools, manage context, and coordinate long-horizon interaction.

paper-2610.29545.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
paper-2610.29545.summary: Linear-attention language models keep their context in a recurrent state of fixed size, where an inference system stores one copy of this state for every sequence it decodes at the same time.

paper-2610.29560.title: From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation
paper-2610.29560.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance across embodied manipulation tasks by unifying visual understanding, language conditioning, and action generation.

paper-2610.29680.title: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking
paper-2610.29680.summary: Using an LLM to generate training data for another is among the most general ways to train one, and it remains common practice.

paper-2610.29722.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation Compositionality
paper-2610.29722.summary: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds large language models in external knowledge.

paper-2610.29784.title: Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting
paper-2610.29784.summary: Most contemporary artificial intelligence (AI) systems are released with frozen parameters and improve through external updates, whereas an ideal system would keep improving from its own experience, a capacity we call recursive self-improvement (RSI).

paper-2610.29932.title: FrontierCS 2: A Benchmark for Computer Science R&D
paper-2610.29932.summary: Can LLM agents make contributions to frontier computer science R&D? We introduce FrontierCS 2, a benchmark of 48 open-ended tasks. We take a paper and the code its authors released and delete the paper's contribution.

paper-2610.29934.title: ToM2Vec: Continuous Theory-of-Mind Tokens for Multi-Agent Coordination
paper-2610.29934.summary: Forming an accurate theory-of-mind (ToM) is key to successful multi-agent collaboration and requires reasoning under uncertainty to capture multiple possible partner states.

paper-2610.29968.title: CulturalRiddles: A Multicultural Benchmark of Riddles
paper-2610.29968.summary: As LLMs expand their language coverage, evaluating how well they understand and represent diverse cultures becomes increasingly important.

paper-2610.29989.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
paper-2610.29989.summary: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk, yet producing plausible continuations does not guarantee that they capture how scenes evolve.

paper-2610.29997.title: DONIC: Generalist Dexterous Bimanual Tracking Control from Human Demonstrations
paper-2610.29997.summary: Despite recent progress in dexterous reference tracking, existing models focus primarily on single-hand manipulation and a limited range of interactions, leaving the bimanual dexterous behaviors common in real life unaddressed.

paper-2610.30023.title: RealMe: Immersive Volumetric Video from Minimal Captures
paper-2610.30023.summary: This paper addresses the problem of creating immersive volumetric videos from sparse and low-resolution capture resources.

paper-2610.30066.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
paper-2610.30066.summary: Uniform diffusion language models (UDLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising sequences of ordinary vocabulary tokens, any of which may be corrupted and subsequently revised.

paper-2610.30090.title: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift
paper-2610.30090.summary: Perimeter triage faces a latency/semantics trade-off: signature engines are fast and format-safe but blind to unseen attacks, while generative models are semantic but slow and produce unparseable output.

paper-2610.30108.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
paper-2610.30108.summary: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics.

paper-2610.30113.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
paper-2610.30113.summary: Quantitative research is an iterative loop: a researcher proposes a market hypothesis, implements it as an executable signal, tests it on historical data, and decides what to keep.

paper-2610.30120.title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
paper-2610.30120.summary: World models turn visual representations into predictions and actions.

paper-2610.30128.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
paper-2610.30128.summary: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. We challenge this de facto design with two diagnostic findings.

paper-2610.30136.title: Agentic World Action Models
paper-2610.30136.summary: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse.
